meta.title: 🚋 Lisbon in 2 Days
meta.subtitle: SEVEN HILLS ON FOOT
meta.where_summary: In and out of Lisbon Airport
meta.all_tip:
🎯 The idea: This isn't a checklist tour of a European capital. It's a walk that rises and falls across seven hills — Lisbon's beauty lives in the turns, in the rattle of the tram, in the faded tiles. Worth wearing your soles down for.

🎬 How it builds: Day 1 starts at the highest point, São Jorge Castle, so you get the lay of the land, then rolls downhill through the Alfama — gravity does half the work. Day 2 shifts to Belém by the river, a flat line from monastery to monument, ending in custard tarts. High to low, old to new, no street walked twice.

🗺️ Why this route: Same hotel both nights, no repacking. Day 1 is downhill on foot; Day 2 rides tram 15 along one straight riverside line, so you never climb the hills twice. Nothing is more than 25 minutes apart.

💡 Practical: Wear grippy shoes — Lisbon's mosaic pavement turns lethal in rain. Book the monastery online; the walk-up queue hits an hour in peak season. Skip August: hot and packed.

stats.label: Budget / person
stats.tooltip: Excludes international flights. Hotel (split for a double) + food + tickets + local transport, with a ±15% band.

highlight_items: Tram 28 (don't queue at the terminus — walk one stop up and you'll actually get a seat)
Belém tarts (go to the original Pastéis de Belém; standing at the counter is cheaper than sitting)
Miradouro hopping (the viewpoints are the soul of this city — go an hour before sunset)
Tile hunting (no two azulejo walls in the Alfama are the same; every alley is a photo)
meta.warning_text: Tram 28 and the Alfama are pickpocket territory — wear your bag on your front. The mosaic pavement is slippery when wet; leave the hard soles at home.

pretrip.visa: Schengen visa required for Chinese passports (~¥800, about 15 working days)
pretrip.sim: eSIM via Airalo (~$8 / 5GB) · local Vodafone SIM about €15
pretrip.currency: €1 ≈ $1.08 · cards accepted almost everywhere, carry a little cash for small shops
pretrip.tipping: Not expected; 5–10% if you enjoyed it

1.title: Day 1 · Downhill from the castle
1.tip: 💡 Taxi straight up to the castle first — everything after that is downhill, which saves your legs.

hotel.highlights: 6 min walk to Avenida metro; 20 min direct to the airport

1.plan_b: 💧 If it rains: the mosaic pavement is treacherous. Swap for the Gulbenkian Museum + Time Out Market + the National Tile Museum — all indoors.

2.title: Day 2 · Belém and the age of sail
2.tip: 💡 Tram 15 runs from Comércio square straight to Belém — leave before 9am to beat the tour groups.
2.plan_b: 💧 If it rains: Belém is exposed. Swap for the Oceanário + Oriente Station + Colombo mall.

pois.name: São Jorge Castle
pois.desc: Highest point in the city — the ramparts give you all of Lisbon and the Tagus in one sweep. Come at opening; once the tour buses land around noon the walls are too packed to photograph. Peacocks roam the inner courtyard.
photo_spots: 📸 East rampart: red rooftops running down to the river
📸 Catch a peacock mid-display in the courtyard

pois.name: Santa Luzia Viewpoint
pois.desc: First terrace on the way down from the castle — wisteria trellis over blue-and-white tilework, the most photogenic corner in Lisbon. Usually a fado busker. Sit a while before moving on.
photo_spots: 📸 Shoot the tiles backlit through the wisteria
📸 Alfama rooftops stacking up from the railing

pois.name: Alfama
pois.desc: The oldest quarter, the only one that survived the 1755 earthquake. There's no itinerary here — head downhill and turn wherever. Laundry lines and tiled walls are the whole point. Pickpockets work this area; bag on your front.
photo_spots: 📸 Laundry lines against a tiled wall in a narrow alley
📸 Press to the wall and catch tram 28 taking the corner
foods: 🐟 Grilled sardines (€12, best at the hole-in-the-wall places)

pois.name: Praça do Comércio
pois.desc: End of the downhill run — a huge yellow square opening onto the river. The light under the arch is best at sunset; €4 gets you onto the roof. Cafés on the east side run about a third cheaper than the west.
photo_spots: 📸 Dead-centre symmetry through the triumphal arch
📸 Sit on the river steps for sunset silhouettes

pois.name: Jerónimos Monastery
pois.desc: World Heritage site and the high point of Manueline architecture; Vasco da Gama is buried here. Book online — the peak-season queue runs to an hour. The church is free, the cloister is ticketed, and the cloister is the reason you came.
photo_spots: 📸 Upper cloister: the arcade running away in perspective
📸 Look straight up at the south portal carving

pois.name: Pastéis de Belém
pois.desc: The 1837 original recipe — the ancestor of every custard tart on earth. The takeaway queue out front is long but there are hundreds of seats inside, so just walk in and grab a table. Dust with cinnamon before eating.
photo_spots: 📸 A plate of tarts against the blue tiled interior
foods: 🥧 Pastel de Belém (€1.40 each — order at least two)

pois.name: Monument to the Discoveries
pois.desc: Riverside monument to the age of exploration. Go up top or you'll only see half of the giant compass rose laid into the pavement below — you need height and distance for that shot.
photo_spots: 📸 From the top, the whole compass rose from above
📸 Backlit profile of the carved figures on the prow

pois.name: Belém Tower
pois.desc: The white stone tower in the river, the departure point of the age of sail. The single spiral stair inside runs on a traffic light — 20 minutes of waiting when it's busy, so if you only want the photo, the bank is enough. At low tide you can walk out to the base.
photo_spots: 📸 Low tide: the tower mirrored at water level
📸 From the causeway with the sun behind it
